claims.quote: Technical due diligence for software acquisitions
claims.statement: The service belongs to the category it names: it performs technical due diligence for software acquisitions — that the core function of the category exists is what is claimed.

claims.quote: the seller's claims checked against the code
claims.statement: The service has a review process that takes the seller's claims about a software product and that product's code and compares the claims against the code.

locations.quote: We check what the software says about itself against what its code actually does.

claims.quote: From a free demo to a signed opinion
claims.statement: The service's engagement spans from a free demo to a delivered signed opinion.

claims.quote: Beta: free claims reviews, limited
claims.statement: The service is currently offered in beta, with claims reviews free of charge and availability limited.

locations.quote: We are in beta. For a limited number of engagements, a claims review is free.

claims.quote: For buyers and advisers of small software companies
claims.statement: The service is aimed at buyers and advisers of small software companies.

claims.quote: A report you can check line by line
claims.statement: The deliverable includes a report the buyer can check line by line.

locations.quote: A report you can check line by line

claims.quote: a private page where you can ask about any part of it
claims.statement: The deliverable includes a private page where the buyer can ask about any part of the report.

locations.quote: a page where you can keep asking
a private page where you can ask about any finding in your own time

claims.quote:
| Part | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| Executive summary | What was examined, and the findings rated material, one line each. |
| What the review showed | Each gap: the claim as written, the verdict, the evidence quoted with its file and lines, the independent check's outcome, and what the gap would change for you. |
| Unsettled claims | Claims the materials cannot settle, why, and how much rests on each. |
| Claims that hold | Listed with their evidence, so the good news is checkable too. |
| Questions for the seller | What to ask to close the gaps the materials left. |
| Appendix | Every claim and its verdict, in document order. |
claims.statement: The report has a fixed shape comprising the six listed parts — executive summary, what the review showed, unsettled claims, claims that hold, questions for the seller, and an appendix — each holding what its row describes.

claims.quote: you name the documents that carry the seller's claims and never see the code
claims.statement: The buyer identifies the documents carrying the seller's claims and is never shown the code.

claims.quote: A small target comes back within days of receiving the materials
claims.statement: A small target's review is returned within days of receiving the materials.

claims.quote: a typical deal in about a week
claims.statement: A typical deal's review is returned in about a week.

claims.quote: Free
claims.statement: The demo tier is offered at no charge.

claims.quote: Read a completed claims review of a small open-source project and ask it questions.
claims.statement: The demo contains a completed claims review of a small open-source project together with an interface a visitor can use to question it.

claims.quote: If you have a repository of your own to evaluate, write to us and we will set you up to run one.
claims.statement: The practice states it will set up a visitor who supplies their own repository to run a claims review on it — a statement of intent about the seller's own activity.

claims.quote: Quoted after intake
claims.statement: The price of a claims review is given as a quote after the intake conversation rather than published.

claims.quote: Every claim in the documents you name, tested against the code
claims.statement: Every claim in the documents the buyer names is tested against the target's code.

claims.quote: signed by a person who stands behind it
claims.statement: The report is signed by a person who takes responsibility for it.

claims.quote: Quoted per engagement
claims.statement: Attested due diligence is priced by quote per engagement rather than published.

locations.quote: A person reads the result and stands behind it.

claims.quote: The claims review, plus a reading of the whole record by someone who has sat on both sides of a deal.
claims.statement: The attested due diligence tier consists of the claims review plus a reading of the whole record by a reviewer who has sat on both sides of a deal.

claims.quote: A signed opinion, and a person on call to your deal team while it matters.
claims.statement: The attested tier delivers a signed opinion and puts a person on call to the buyer's deal team for the duration that matters.

claims.quote: Advisers and buyers of software businesses in the $1M to $5M range, at the point where the seller's description of the product is the main thing on the table.
claims.statement: The service is aimed at advisers and buyers of software businesses in the $1M to $5M range, at the pre-letter-of-intent stage.

claims.quote: A claims review sits a rung below a full technical due diligence: narrower, quicker, and priced so it can be done before the letter of intent rather than after.
claims.statement: A claims review is narrower, quicker and priced lower than a full technical due diligence, such that it can be done before the letter of intent rather than after.

claims.quote: The same method serves a developer choosing an open-source dependency on the strength of its README; the free demo is that case.
claims.statement: The method works when the only claim source is a README, and the free demo demonstrates exactly that case.

claims.quote: It is not a penetration test, not a review of code quality or architecture, and not legal advice.
claims.statement: The service excludes penetration testing, code quality or architecture review, and legal advice.

claims.quote: It reads the code
claims.statement: The review reads the target's code.

claims.quote: It reports the state of each claim and what a gap would change for you.
claims.statement: The report states the status of each claim and the consequence each gap would have for the buyer.

claims.quote: A short conversation about what you are evaluating and why: what you already know, what would change your mind, and, for a deal, what would move the price or end it.
claims.statement: The engagement begins with an intake conversation covering what is being evaluated, what is already known, and what would change the decision or the price.

claims.quote: and then each one is tested against the code and the documents supplied
claims.statement: Each frozen claim is then tested against the code and the documents the buyer supplied.

claims.quote: twice, and looked at again when the two readings differ
claims.statement: Every gap is rated twice, and the rating is re-examined when the two readings disagree.

claims.quote: with the working record behind every answer
claims.statement: The private question page provides access to the working record underlying each answer to a buyer's question.

claims.quote: The reading is done by language models
claims.statement: The review reading is performed by language models.

claims.quote: but not by asking one a question and taking its word
claims.statement: The reading is not a single model's unverified answer taken on trust.

claims.quote: The models work inside a fixed procedure that keeps the list of claims separate from the verdicts, keeps every search and every file opened, and refuses a finding it cannot cite.
claims.statement: The models operate inside a fixed procedure that separates the claim list from the verdicts, retains a record of every search and every file opened, and refuses findings that cannot be cited.

claims.quote: The report says on every line which part was machine and which was judgment.
claims.statement: Every line of the report attributes its content to machine work or to human judgment.

claims.quote: Machine drafts. A person confirms and signs. The report tells you which is which.
claims.statement: Same assertion as the report-attribution claim: machines draft, a person confirms and signs, and the report distinguishes the two.

claims.quote: the seller's claims checked against the code
claims.statement: In operation, the seller's claims about a software product are actually checked against that product's actual code.

claims.quote: Read a completed claims review of a small open-source project and ask it questions.
claims.statement: A visitor to the demo can ask questions about the completed claims review and receive answers to them.
